derivation_notes: The parent already allows substrate occupancy to reshape the acidic protonation branch via an occupancy-dependent Hill-like factor; here the same microstate-redistribution logic is extended to the alkaline inactivation branch. This modifies the high-pH term by combining the baseline alkaline steepness with an occupancy correction before applying the exponential map, so substrate can change alkaline-flank curvature as well as its midpoint.
change_summary: Relaxed the assumption that the alkaline transition has a fixed apparent steepness n_high. The successor lets substrate occupancy alter alkaline steepness through delta_n_high*S/(K_M + S), producing substrate-dependent broadening or sharpening of the high-pH activity loss.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The alkaline transition is represented by a single fixed apparent Hill coefficient n_high that does not change with substrate occupancy or microstate redistribution.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Coupled protonation microstates or conformational substates linked to the alkaline catalytic group can make the high-pH inactivation step non-ideal, and substrate binding can redistribute those microstates so the alkaline flank steepness changes with occupancy.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when delta_n_high = 0, so the effective alkaline Hill coefficient becomes the constant n_high.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed substrate concentration, pH modulates activity through one productive protonation window bounded by a low-pH and a high-pH transition, so the log-rate profile is controlled by a single pair of apparent ionization flanks with substrate-dependent shifts but only one central active phase.
response_change.child_relation: Allow the alkaline loss-of-activity transition to be non-ideal as well, so substrate can reshape not only the window position but also the upper-flank curvature and shoulder/broadening behavior through coupled protonation microstates on the basic side.
response_change.observable_effect: Across substrate levels, the high-pH side can change from a simple single-slope falloff to a broader or sharper alkaline shoulder while the acidic side remains similar, altering the pH-profile width and asymmetry in a way the parent cannot match with one fixed alkaline steepness.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Most visible when pH samples extend through and above the alkaline activity-loss flank and substrate occupancy varies appreciably from low to near-saturating values, i.e. S spanning values below and around K_M so theta changes substantially.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying pH at several substrate levels already reveals substrate-dependent movement of the active window; in holdout, the same mechanism predicts that the upper-flank curvature and apparent width also change with substrate rather than only translating rigidly.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the alkaline non-ideality vanishes, e.g. the added high-pH steepness correction tends to zero and the effective alkaline Hill coefficient returns to the parent's constant n_high.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Coupled protonation microstates or conformational substates linked to the alkaline catalytic group can make the high-pH inactivation step non-ideal, and substrate binding can redistribute those microstates so the alkaline flank steepness changes with occupancy.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because substrate occupancy and alkaline pH displacement are first combined into an effective steepness-weighted base-drive and only then passed through the 10** nonlinear map, changing the shape of the observable pH-rate curve rather than merely rescaling it.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The alkaline transition has a fixed apparent Hill-like steepness n_high, with substrate affecting only its apparent pKa position.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The alkaline transition steepness is itself occupancy dependent because substrate binding redistributes coupled alkaline protonation microstates.
evolution_contract.before_fragment: k_cat*E_total*S/((K_M + S)*(1 + 10**((n_low0 + delta_n_low*S/(K_M + S))*(pKa_low - pH - delta_pKa_low*S/(K_M + S))) + 10**(n_high*(pH - pKa_high - delta_pKa_high*S/(K_M + S)))))
evolution_contract.after_fragment: k_cat*E_total*S/((K_M + S)*(1 + 10**((n_low0 + delta_n_low*S/(K_M + S))*(pKa_low - pH - delta_pKa_low*S/(K_M + S))) + 10**((n_high + delta_n_high*S/(K_M + S))*(pH - pKa_high - delta_pKa_high*S/(K_M + S)))))
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Setting delta_n_high = 0 exactly recovers the parent expression.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed temperature and ionic strength, compare pH-rate profiles at low substrate and near-saturating substrate. If measurements cover the alkaline flank, the successor permits the upper-flank descent to broaden or sharpen with S while the acidic side remains approximately governed by the same parent branch; the parent with one shared parameter set can only shift that upper flank horizontally through delta_pKa_high and cannot reproduce substrate-dependent alkaline curvature changes.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all parent parameters still leaves one constant n_high for every substrate level, so the parent can change alkaline midpoint position but not make the high-pH falloff have different apparent steepness or shoulder width at different S values with the same global parameter set. Because the scored target v_pH itself changes shape across supplied pH and S conditions, this is not absorbable as an auxiliary-only modification.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Most visible when pH samples extend through and above the alkaline activity-loss flank and substrate occupancy varies appreciably from low to near-saturating values, i.e. S spanning values below and around K_M so theta changes substantially.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying pH at several substrate levels already reveals substrate-dependent movement of the active window; in holdout, the same mechanism predicts that the upper-flank curvature and apparent width also change with substrate rather than only translating rigidly.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the alkaline non-ideality vanishes, e.g. the added high-pH steepness correction tends to zero and the effective alkaline Hill coefficient returns to the parent's constant n_high.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current law assumes the high-pH inactivation branch has a fixed idealized steepness except for a horizontal pKa shift, even though the low-pH branch already allows microstate-coupled non-ideality and substrate-dependent reshaping.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The alkaline transition is represented by a single fixed apparent Hill coefficient n_high that does not change with substrate occupancy or microstate redistribution.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Coupled protonation microstates or conformational substates linked to the alkaline catalytic group can make the high-pH inactivation step non-ideal, and substrate binding can redistribute those microstates so the alkaline flank steepness changes with occupancy.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent maps inputs to rate through one productive pH window with substrate-dependent boundary shifts, but on the alkaline side it enforces a single-phase falloff shape because n_high is fixed for all S. A realistic next refinement is to relax that idealization and let the alkaline branch have occupancy-dependent non-ideal steepness, paralleling the already admitted low-pH microstate complexity. The varied conditions are pH and substrate concentration, with temperature and ionic strength fixed as stated. The concrete contrast is at two substrate regimes, one with S much less than K_M and one with S comparable to or greater than K_M: the parent can shift the alkaline midpoint through delta_pKa_high but cannot, with one shared parameter set, make the high-pH descent broaden at one S and sharpen at another while keeping the acidic branch approximately unchanged. This is an actual target-mapping change because v_pH itself versus supplied pH and S changes shape, not merely an unobserved auxiliary quantity. The effect is admissible when measurements cover the alkaline flank; if data never reach above the upper apparent pKa, the refinement would be weakly identifiable, which is a limitation rather than a reason to invent another mechanism.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Combine declared quantities before applying a nonlinear map, such as relative speed followed by quadratic drag.

scenario_text: The catalytic activity of an enzyme depends on whether key catalytic groups are protonated in the productive configuration. Activity is measured at independently sampled pH values and substrate concentrations while temperature and ionic strength are fixed. The response reflects rapid protonation equilibria coupled to substrate turnover, not a temporal change in enzyme abundance.
